title: Welcome back, choom!
text: With update 2.0, there is a number of new features and changes you should know about before you dive in.

title: Consumable Items
text:
Consumable items such as grenades, inhalers and injectors have been reworked. They now have charges and can be used as long as there are charges remaining. Number of charges is indicated by a number on the item icon.
Charges refill over time.

title: Stamina
text:
Stamina now affects both melee and ranged combat.

Shooting range weapons drains Stamina. The lower the Stamina the worse the weapon's accuracy and handling.

For melee combat, if Stamina reaches critical levels or runs out, damage and attack speed are decreased.

title: Breach Protocol
text: Breach Protocol is no longer avialable as a quickhack option versus enemies or other characters in general. It is still usable on access points, computer terminals, certain shards etc.

title: Weaponized Vehicles
text:
Some cars are equipped with various weaponry, like machine guns or missile launchers.

Hold <Input context="VehicleDriverCombat" actionName="UI_FakeRangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to shoot.
You will lock-on enemies automatically by default - this setting can be changed in the Settings menu.

Press <Input context="VehicleDriveMountedWeapons" actionName="MountedWeapons_SwitchWeapons" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to switch weapons.
Hold <Input context="VehicleDriverCombat" actionName="UI_FakeCameraAim" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to aim manually.
Press <Input context="VehicleDriverCombat" actionName="ExitCombatMode" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to exit vehicle combat.

title: Vehicle Combat
text:
Drawing your weapon while driving enables combat, allowing you to drive and shoot at the same time. You can use pistols and submachine guns when sitting behind the wheel.

Shoot: hold <Input context="VehicleDriverCombat" actionName="UI_FakeRangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

By default, your aim will lock onto enemies automatically. This setting can be changed in the Settings menu.

Manual Aim: hold <Input context="VehicleDriverCombat" actionName="UI_FakeCameraAim" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Exit Combat: <Input context="VehicleDriverCombat" actionName="ExitCombatMode" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Character Reset
text: Due to significant changes in gameplay mechanics, your Perks have been reset and your Perk Points have been refunded, allowing you to rebuild your character however you like.

title: Quickhacking Cameras
text: To quickhack a camera, you must first scan it using your optical cyberware. This gives you several options such as taking control of the camera, shifting its field of vision or shutting it down.

title: Elevators
text:
Elevators can give you access to other floors within a building.
There may be times when certain floors are temporarily inaccessible to you – for example, if your companion did not accompany you into the elevator or if you have not progressed far enough into the story, among other possible reasons.

title: Fistfights
text: Your fists can be dangerous weapons. In fistfights, you can use them to both strike your enemies and block their attacks.

title: Weapon Store
text: A vendor's shop screen displays the list of items available at that location. Simply select an item to buy it, provided you have sufficient money.

title: Shooting Range
text: Shoot at the targets to score points. Try this out if you want to test weapon or just feel like unwinding.

title: Entering Stealth Mode
text: To crouch and enter Stealth Mode, press <Input actionName="Crouch" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: !WIP
text: !WIP

title: Playstyles
text: How you overcome adversity depends solely on you. You can fight head-on with guns blazing, sneak through enemy hideouts without tripping an alarm, and/or use an arsenal of techie and netrunner skills. Remember to enjoy exploring alternative methods to get the job done until you find a style that suits you.

title: Attribute Requirements
text: As you level up your Attributes, you may unlock new interactions with the environment that allow you to take different approaches when completing Jobs and Gigs.

title: Movement Tutorial
text: Movement, minimap, and map marker tutorial.

title: Netrunner on the Line
text: During this job, you will have your netrunner, T-Bug, on the phone to help guide you through its different stages.

title: Switching Between View Modes in Braindances
text: To switch between Editor (third-person view) and Playback (first-person view) in braindances, press <Input actionName="BdCameraToggle" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Unpausing Braindances
text: To pause or resume the braindance, press <Input actionName="Pause" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Pausing Braindances
text: To pause the braindance, press <Input actionName="Pause" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Rewinding Braindances
text: Press and hold <Input actionName="PlayBackward" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> to rewind a braindance. The longer you hold, the faster it rewinds.

title: Fast-forwarding Braindances
text: Press and hold <Input actionName="PlayForward" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> to fast-forward a braindance. The longer you hold, the faster it fast-forwards.

title: Restarting Braindances
text: To restart the braindance, hold <Input actionName="Restart" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Clue Indicators
text: When an important clue is scanned, it will become marked on the recording track at the top of the screen.

title: Braindance Layers
text: To switch between available braindance layers, press <Input actionName="SwitchLayer" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Braindance Layers and Clues
text: Clues can only be scanned during a braindance if they are being actively perceived by the person recording. Rewind the braindance to scan the screen.

title: Finding Clues in Braindances
text: You can only scan a clue during moments when it's perceivable by the person recording the braindance.

title: Exiting Braindances
text: To exit the braindance, press <Input actionName="ExitBraindance" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Quickhacking Doors
text: Select the quickhack from the quick-access menu. If you don't have the necessary Skill level, the option will be unusable and grayed out. For this task, T-Bug gave you a special shard that imitates a cyberdeck.

title: Panzer: Movement
text: Panzer's movement is completely unique and is more reliant on player movement than standard road vehicles. Instead of using gas and brake pedals, the Basilisk uses biometric thumb data for movement. Use [Left Joystick] to maneuver the Panzer.

title: Panzer: Cannon
text:
The primary cannon can rotate 360 degrees and has two modes of fire:
1) Standard automatic fire. The double-barrels alternate fire as long as the trigger is pressed. Press [R2] to enter the mode and hold it to sustain fire.
2) Precision strikes. Hold [L2] to enter this mode. Holding [L2] allows you to fire both barrels simultaneously. This mode provides greater precision and less dispersion, but reduces the rate of fire.

title: Panzer: Missile Launcher
text: The Basilisk is equipped with smart missiles that home in on your target. Press <Input context="VehicleTankDrive" actionName="ShootSecondary" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to fire a homing missile to attack your selected target.

title: Panzer: Countermeasures
text: Press <Input actionName="ShootTertiary" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to fire smoke missiles in a semi-circle around the tank. The missiles explode shortly after launch and leave clouds of electrically charged smoke suspended in the air, which obstruct enemy field of vision and incapacitates enemies in the blast zone.

title: Panzer: Afterburner
text: To gain a temporary afterburner boost, press [A].

title: Militech Basilisk Armored Transport (AKA Panzer)
text:
The Basilisk is a unique vehicle in the world of Cyberpunk 2077. Compared to other vehicles, the Basilisk has:
No visible suspension when using jet rockets for lift,
Full-range multi-directional movement,
Rotational movement while stationary,
Combat capabilities (some models)
Unque piloting experience,
Unique command input, whereby it's possible to pilot and use combat systems simultaneously in armed models.

title: Panzer: Camera Rotation
text:
Use [Right Stick] to control the camera.
When inside the panzer, [Right Stick] aims the cannon.
When outside, [Right Stick] rotates the entire panzer, which always adjusts to the camera's position.

title: Vehicle Combat
text: To enter Vehicle Combat Mode, use the quick-access menu to select a weapon.

title: Scanning Clues
text: For the purposes of this tutorial, the recording has been stopped the right time for you to scan the clue. During normal gameplay, you will have to stop the recording at the necessary time on your own.

title: Switching Cameras
text: To connect between two available cameras, press <Input context="DeviceControl" actionName="SwitchDeviceNext" color="MainColors.Blue"></> or <Input context="DeviceControl" actionName="SwitchDevicePrevious" color="MainColors.Blue"></>.

title: Thermal Layer
text: The thermal layer is now unlocked. To switch between layers, press <Input actionName="SwitchLayer" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Camera Movement
text: In braindance editing mode you can move the camera freely around the scene.

title: Interior Manager
text: The Interior Manager allows you to customize your apartment. Use [ToggleVision] to exit.

title: Dialogues and Scenes
text:
In the dialogue system of Cyberpunk 2077, you can look around freely, decide whom to interact with, and interact with various objects. If you want to make a conversation more interesting, pay special attention to your surroundings.

Use <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> / <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to scroll through available dialogue options and automatically change your view.

Confirm your dialogue choice with <Input actionName="ChoiceApply" color="MainColors.Blue"></>

title: Driving
text:
Accelerate with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Steer with <Input context="MovementActions" actionName="MoveX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Brake with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Decelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Exit the vehicle with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Exit" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Ranged Combat: Basics
text:
Shoot with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>
Aim with <Input actionName="RangedADS" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Reload with <Input actionName="Reload" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Holster your weapon by double-tapping <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Netrunner
text: The optical cyberware you have installed is equipped with modules for analyzing networks and their weak points. These scans provide valuable information about your surroundings and possible threats.

title: Scanning
text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Hold</> <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">to use your scanner.</>

title: Job Clues
text: Objects highlighted in yellow while scanning contain valuable info to help you with the current job.

title: Grappling
text: Sneaking up to an unaware enemy will give you the option to <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">grapple</> them with <Input actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Lethal and Non-Lethal Takedowns
text: You can choose how to deal with enemies. Sometimes it's enough to perform a non-lethal takedown.

title: Carrying Bodies
text: You can lift and carry dead, unconscious or otherwise incapacitated enemies by pressing and holding <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice2_Hold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Double Takedown
text: You can use the help of a companion to execute a double takedown – the perfect strategy for quietly disposing of two enemies simultaneously. Grab one of the indicated enemies.

title: Distractions
text:
Quickhacks can help you distract enemies.

If you create a distraction, such as a sound, nearby enemies will be forced to investigate the source of it. This will give you a good opportunity to incapacitate them or sneak by them.

title: Using Your Phone
text: To access your phone menu, hold <Input actionName="PhoneInteract" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Stash
text: Your Stash is a secure system for storing equipment and can be accessed from all of your available safehouses and vehicles. For example, if you store something in your car trunk, you'll be able to access it from your apartment later on.

title: Gigs
text: Gigs are tasks offered by fixers in each of Night City's districts. When you enter a district, you will receive a text message from the local fixer that details all of the available Gigs, automatically marking their locations on your map. When you approach a Gig location closely enough, you will receive another text message with a task brief and your Journal will update with the information.

title: Vehicles: Calling
text: You can call your active vehicle to your current location with <Input actionName="CallVehicle" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>

title: Vehicles
text:
Accelerate with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Steer with <Input context="MovementActions" actionName="MoveX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Brake with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Decelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Exit the vehicle with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Exit" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Cyberware
text:
Cybernetic implants are mechanical replacements for the organic parts of your body. They can give you superhuman-like abilities which can improve your combat capability and help you survive in hazardous conditions.

Although a common practice in 2077, the installation of cyberware is still an invasive, and sometimes dangerous, medical procedure. Only specialists known as ripperdocs are trusted to install cyberware safely.

title: Ripperdoc
text:
Though a common practice, cyberware installation is still a dangerous and invasive procedure which can only be performed by qualified specialists: ripperdocs. There are several ripperdocs operating throughout Night City who offer a variety of different cyberware upgrades.

Select your desired cybernetic upgrade from the list and enjoy your new abilities.

title: Scanning People
text:
Scanning people with your optical cyberware can provide you with a lot of useful information, such as how strong an enemy might be, who is in their crew, or what type of weapon they use.

As a skilled netrunner, you can see a list of quickhacks which you can use against your enemies.

title: Fast Travel
text: Traveling around Night City allows you to discover and unlock Dataterms, which will then become available Fast Travel locations for you to use later.

title: Combat
text: Quickly draw a weapon with <Input actionName="HolsterUnholster" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, or draw your most recently used weapon with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>. Cycle your weapons with <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Ranged Combat
text:
Shoot with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Aim with <Input actionName="RangedADS" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Reload with <Input actionName="Reload" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Switch to melee combat with <Input actionName="QuickMelee" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Melee Combat
text:
Fast Attack: <Input actionName="MeleeAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Strong Attack: hold <Input actionName="MeleeAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Block: <Input actionName="MeleeBlock" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Combat Gadgets
text:
Arm and cook a grenade by holding <Input actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> then release the button to throw it.
Press <Input actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to quickly throw a grenade.
Hold <Input actionName="GadgetWheel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the Combat Gadgets menu and select an item you want to use.

title: Consumables
text: Hostile cameras that can detect you have  <Rich color="F3B23F" style="Bold">orange</> scanning beams, while friendly ones have <Rich color="67e04f" style="Bold">green</> beams. Cameras will detect you if you enter their field of vision, but they do not register noise.

title: Crafting
text: Crafting allows you to assemble items based on Crafting Specs you can buy and find around Night City.
When in mid-air, you automatically grab onto or vault over nearby ledges.

title: Vendors
text: Panel Details

title: Movement
text: Your maximum movement speed can be changed depending on which Perks and cyberware you have at your disposal.

title: Crouching
text: While crouched, you can move silently.

title: Vaulting
text: While running, you can leap over surfaces that can also be used as cover.

title: Ladders
text: When you approach a ladder, you will automatically grab onto it and begin climbing up or down. Climbing down a ladder requires pressing <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Sprinting
text: You can climb faster with <Input actionName="ToggleSprint" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Swimming: Movement
text: While in water, you can swim upward with <Input actionName="Jump" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> or dive down with <Input actionName="ToggleCrouch" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Swimming: Oxygen
text: Without access to air, you will begin to suffocate and receive damage, which can eventually result in death.

title: Shooting: Drawing Your Weapon
text: In some areas of Night City, drawing your weapon might be considered a threat. Be mindful of how others around you might react.

title: Shooting Tip #2
text: Shooting while moving is less accurate than when in stable position.

title: Shooting: Reloading Tip #1
text: Reloading an empty ammo clip takes longer than reloading a weapon with a bullet in the chamber.

title: Shooting: Tech Weapons
text: Tech weapons were built for precision and their ability to pierce through solid cover.

title: Shooting: Smart Weapons
text: While Smart Link is equipped, Smart weapons fire homing rounds that will bend your bullets' trajectory mid-flight.

title: Melee Combat: Counterattacks
text: Timing a block just before getting hit will allow you to deflect your enemy's attack and automatically deal them a counterblow.

title: Vehicles: Combat
text:
Draw Weapon: <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Holster Weapon and Return to Seat: double-tap <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

As the passenger, drawing your weapon allows you to lean out the window and use your entire arsenal of equipped ranged weapons.

Shoot: <Input context="Combat" actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>

title: Text Messages
text: Press <Input actionName="NotificationOpen" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to view the conversation thread.

title: Timed Dialogue Options
text: Some dialogue options are only available for a limited time. The option will disappear when the time bar runs out.

title: Movement
text: Move with <Input actionName="UI_FakeMovement" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and look around with <Input actionName="UI_FakeCamera" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Job Objectives
text: Active job objectives are marked with <Image id="MappinIcons.QuestMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75" color="MainColors.Gold"></> on your HUD and minimap.

title: Ladders: Hint
text: Approach the ladder to automatically begin climbing it.

title: Scanning a Device
text: Use your optical cyberware to scan a device in order to find weak points in the network to which it is connected.

title: Access Point
text: Access Points are your way into local networks, allowing you to gather valuable data that may yield rewards in some parts of the game.

title: Access Point Interaction
text: Press <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to begin quickhacking.

title: Quickhacking: Hints
text: A special <Rich color="MainColors.MildGreen">highlight</> indicates devices that have vulnerabilities you can exploit.

title: Quickhacking: Interaction
text: To begin quickhacking, look at a device and scan it by holding <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Breach Protocol: Hints
text: By scanning devices with your optical cyberware, you can learn additional information about them.

title: Breach Protocol: Daemons
text: This is the list of daemons and the character sequences required to upload each one.

title: Cost of Quickhacking a Device
text: Quickhacks use up a portion of your cyberdeck's RAM when performed. Used RAM units recover over time.

title: Noise
text: Noise from your movement can alert enemies to your presence. Running, jumping and using weapons will increase your risk of detection.

title: Crouching
text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Press</> <Input actionName="ToggleCrouch" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">to crouch and move quietly.</>

title: Patrols
text: Enemies that are unaware of your presence will continue their routines. <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Pay attention to their behavior patterns and use what you learn to sneak around them.</>

title: Installing Quickhacks
text:
Your cyberdeck allows you to use the environment to your advantage by installing and uploading quickhacks.
Your currently installed quickhacks can distract enemies by sabotaging a variety of devices.
Quickhacks can be installed or uninstalled in your inventory.
You can get new quickhacks from from vendors, job rewards, loot-boxes or through crafting.

title: Selecting a Weapon
text: Quickly draw a weapon using <Input actionName="HolsterUnholster" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, or draw your most recently used weapon with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>. Cycle your weapons with <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>. Hold <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the quick-access menu and either draw a weapon assigned to a slot or holster your currently equipped weapon.

title: Crafting Specs
text: This list contains all Crafting Specs that you have learned. To craft an item, select the Crafting Spec that corresponds to it.

title: Crafting Preview
text: A detailed description of all items that can be crafted.

title: Crafting: Components
text: This list shows all the components required to craft the selected Crafting Spec as well as the components you currently have available.

title: Upgrading
text: Upgrades to weapons can improve their statistics and quality, allowing you to use them for longer.

title: Upgrading Weapons
text: List of upgradable weapons.

title: Upgrading: Preview
text: Selected weapons will display the stats of the upgraded version.

title: Upgrading: Components
text: This list shows all the components required to perform the selected upgrade as well as the components you currently have available.

title: Character Skills
text:
Each Attribute contains a set of Skills.

Both Attributes and Skills provide different bonuses depending on your style of play.

Skill levels increase as you perform activities associated with them.

The maximum level of a Skill is limited by the level of the Attribute that it belongs to.

title: Character Perks
text:
Each Skill contains a set of Perks. Perks are special abilities that allow you to play according to your preferred playstyle.

With each character level you gain, you will receive points that you can spend on Perks of your choice by pressing <Input actionName="ChoiceApply" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Character Stats
text: Here, you will find detailed information about all of your character's statistics.

title: Database Shards
text: The content of all datashards you find will be added to this tab.

title: Text Message Screen
text: On this screen, browse conversation histories, read unread messages, and send replies to active conversations.

title: Shooting: Cover
text: While aiming from behind cover, part of your body will lean out and become exposed.

title: Melee Combat: Stamina and Fatigue
text: Consecutive attacks will deplete your Stamina, causing a decrease in attack speed.

title: Grappling Enemies 1
text: Grappled enemies will eventually escape your grip after a short while.

title: Grappling Enemies 3
text: OUTDATED The Perk "Athletics_Area_01_Perk_2" allows you to kick grappled enemies.

title: Dumping Bodies
text: You can hide dead and unconscious enemies in certain places. Doing so will help you avoid detection by other enemies.

title: Welcome to Cyberpunk 2077!
text:
First time in Night City? Pay close attention to the tutorials to learn more about the basic mechanics of the game.

Or, if you're already an experienced edgerunner, feel free to disable hints.

Go to the Database at any time during the game to access tutorials as well as to read up on the most important topics of Cyberpunk 2077.

title: Attribute Requirements
text: If an Attribute Requirement appears in red, it means your Attribute level is not high enough to perform the action.

title: Smart Weapons
text:
Smart weapons require a Smart Link to unlock the full potential of their targeting systems.
To install one, be sure to visit your trusty ripperdoc.

title: Tech Weapons: Piercing
text: Tech weapons allow you to charge up powerful shots that can pierce light cover to hit enemies.

title: Ricochet Weapons
text: You can control the trajectory of bullet ricochets with Power weapons if you have Ballistic Coprocessor cyberware installed in your hands.

title: Enemy Netrunners
text: A hostile netrunner is trying to breach your system! You must neutralize them to stop the hack. You can use your scanner to highlight the connection between you and the netrunner, helping you to locate them.

title: Enemy Netrunners: Quickhacking
text: Hostile netrunners may use their allies or cameras as proxies. If you find yourself within their range, you may become the target of a netrunner attack.

title: Equipping Combat Gadgets
text: Assign a grenade to the Combat Gadget quickslot in your inventory so you can make easy use of it during combat.

title: Using Combat Gadgets
text: Arm a grenade by holding <Input actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then release the button to throw it. Press <Input actionName="CancelChargingCG" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to disarm and stow the grenade. Press <Input actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to quickly throw a grenade.

title: Using Consumables
text: Press <Input actionName="UseConsumable" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to use the Consumable item.

title: Viewing Job Objectives
text: You can switch between active job objectives with <Input actionName="CycleObjectives" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Vehicle Combat as a Passenger
text:
As a passenger, you can wield a Pistol or Revolver.

Aim with <Input actionName="RangedADS" color="MainColors.Blue"></>
Shoot with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="MainColors.Blue" hold="Hide"></>
Reload with <Input actionName="Reload" color="MainColors.Blue"></>

title: Cover
text: Crouching behind cover can shield you from enemy fire.

title: Stealth
text: When you enter an enemy's line of sight, their Alert Indicator will begin to fill. <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Find cover to avoid detection.</>

title: Damage
text: You're injured. If your Health falls to zero, you die.

title: Using Consumables
text:
When you pick up a consumable, it will automatically be added to the Consumable quickslot in your inventory if empty.

<Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Press</> <Input actionName="UseConsumable" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">now to use one to restore Health.</>

title: Targeting Enemies
text: Enemies appear as red dots on the minimap. You can also press <Input actionName="Ping" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to highlight their positions.

title: Security Systems
text: Keep an eye out for security systems, such as turrets and surveillance cameras, which can trigger alarms to alert enemies to your position.

title: Field of Vision
text: Hostile cameras that can detect you have  <Rich color="F3B23F" style="Bold">orange</> scanning beams, while friendly ones have <Rich color="67e04f" style="Bold">green</> beams. Cameras will detect you if you enter their field of vision, but they do not register noise.

title: Assault in Progress
text: To complete this NCPD Scanner Hustle, defeat all enemies and collect the loot, or collect the loot unnoticed.

title: Reported Crime
text:
Neutralize the criminals to receive your reward from the NCPD.
Then search the area to find some illegally stashed loot and complete this NCPD Scanner Hustle.

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting
text: Neutralize the cyberpsycho.

title: Hidden Gems
text: While exploring Night City and the surrounding area, you may come across valuable containers with loot. They might be tricky to find, since they're not marked on your minimap.

title: Suspected Organized Crime Activity
text: Neutralize all enemies in the area.

title: !OUTDATED
text: !OUTDATED

title: Stealth and Noise
text: Staying out of sight isn't always enough. Enemies can hear you, so try to avoid making noise while sneaking.

title: Panzer: Movement
text:
Accelerate/Decelerate: <Input context="VehicleTankDrive" actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Strafe Left/Right: <Input context="VehicleTankDrive" actionName="TurnX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Rotate: <Input context="CameraMovement" actionName="UI_FakeCamera" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Panzer: Primary Weapon
text: Press <Input context="VehicleTankDrive" actionName="ShootPrimary" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to lock on and keep holding to fire.

title: Panzer: Homing Missiles
text: Tap <Input context="VehicleTankDrive" actionName="ShootSecondary" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to fire a homing missiles. Hold <Input context="VehicleTankDrive" actionName="ShootSecondary" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to stay locked on to targets.

title: Panzer: Countermeasures
text: Use <Input context="VehicleTankDrive" actionName="ShootTertiary" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to deploy countermeasures.

title: Training
text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">To continue training, select a training module.</>

title: Quickacking Enemies
text: You can hack enemies the same way you hack devices. Hold <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to activate your scanner, then aim it at the guard and press <Input actionName="OpenQuickHackPanel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to access the quickhack menu.

title: Distractions
text: Use the Call In quickhack to lure one guard to the other.

title: Chaining Quickhacks
text: You can use multiple quickhacks simultaneously to gain an advantage. Use the Call In quickhack to lure two guards to the same place.

title: Lethal Quickhacks
text: Use the Detonate Grenade quickhack on the other guard to eliminate both enemies at the same time.

title: Quickhacking: Duration
text: The icon displayed on hacked devices indicates how long the quickhack will remain active. For example, it could show how long a Distract quickhack will hold the enemies' attention.

title: NCPD Scanner Hustles
text: With Viktor's help, you have access to the NCPD network which allows you to reach crime scenes before the police have a chance to investigate.

title: Tagging
text: To tag a target with your optical cyberware, <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">activate your scanner and aim at your chosen target with </><Input actionName="VisionHold" color="MainColors.Blue"></>, <Rich color="MainColors.Gold"> then press </> <Input actionName="TagButton" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Leveling Up Skills
text: Using a Skill will increase your proficiency in it.

title: Ranged Combat
text:
Shoot with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>
Aim with <Input actionName="RangedADS" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Reload with <Input actionName="Reload" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Change weapons with <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Quickhacking
text: Hold <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to activate your scanner, then aim at the screen and press <Input actionName="OpenQuickHackPanel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the quickhack menu.

title: Quickhacking
text: This screen shows your cyberdeck's installed quickhacks. If a quickhack is faded out, it means it cannot be used at this time.

title: Quickhacking: Cyberdeck RAM
text: The number of quickhacks you can use is limited by the amount of RAM units on your cyberdeck. Used RAM units recover over time.

title: Quickhacking: Distractions
text: Distract enemies by turning on the TV, forcing them to come over to investigate.

title: Environmental Takedowns
text:
You can defeat enemies and dump their bodies in one swift motion if they are located near body disposal locations.

<Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Try it out by sneaking up to the guard and pressing</> <Input actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Quickhacking: ICEpick
text: Sometimes the RAM cost of a quickhack will exceed your cyberdeck's available RAM units. You can reduce the cost by using the ICEpick daemon first. Use it now.

title: Grappling Strong Enemies
text: Enemies at a much higher level than you (marked with a <Image color="MainColors.CombatRed" id="UIIcon.q000_tutorial_icon_boss" align="bottom" width="70" height="70"></> icon) are able to free themselves from your grapple more easily. Defeating them is extremely difficult, so proceed with caution.

title: test
text: Press<Input actionName="Reload" color="0099ff"></>to reload

title: Street Cred
text: Performing certain actions will reward you with Street Cred. Build your Street Cred to make a name for yourself in the Night City underworld. Doing so will open up new opportunities.

title: Buying Items
text: Buy an item with <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Selling Items
text: Sell an unwanted item with <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Cyberware Slots
text: Select one of the cyberware slots to install a new implant.

title: Ripperdoc Inventory
text: This list shows all cyberware the ripperdoc has on offer as well as what you already own. Select and install an implant with <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Fast Travel
text: You can go to a Fast Travel location <Image id="MappinIcons.FastTravelMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75" color="MainColors.StrongFastTravel"></> by placing your cursor on it and pressing <Input context="UIShared" actionName="world_map_menu_fast_travel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Inventory: Items
text: Press <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> on a slot in your inventory to use or change the item assigned to it.

title: Inventory Window
text: The Inventory screen shows the list of owned items which you can equip. Press <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> on an item to assign it to the approprate slot.

title: Ui_inventory_mods
text: Mods are used to improve the statistics of clothing and weapons.

title: Installing Mods
text: Some of your equipment will have mod slots built in which you can use to make improvements. Select a mod slot with <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> in order to filter the mods you have available for the equipment in that slot.

title: Breach Protocol
text: Compile the appropriate sequences of Data Nodes for the listed daemons in order to gain the corresponding benefits. The list of daemons available for you to exploit will increase as your character develops.
To successfully upload a daemon through a network backdoor, you must fill the Buffer with the required characters from the Code Matrix. You must select them in the proper sequence.

title: Breach Protocol: Matrix Columns
text: Now you can select a character from the active column, thus adding it to your Buffer and activating the row it belongs to. This allows you to select other characters in that row.

title: OBSOLETE
text: OBSOLETE

title: Tutorial_crafting_main
text: Pick blueprint from list and craft item using [UI APPLY]

title: Tutorial_upgrading_main
text: Upgrading increases quality of an item. Select item from the list and upgrade using [UI_Apply]

title: Breaking Into Vehicles
text: You can bypass the locks of parked vehicles if you meet the Technical Ability Attribute Requirement. But remember: Police may respond to an attempted vehicle break-in.

title: Police: Introduction
text: Any illegal activity, such as theft or attacking civilians, will result in the NCPD placing a bounty on you. The police will send a patrol to the crime scene, and the strength of their response will be proportional to the size of the bounty. To lose the police, move away from the crime scene and lay low for a while.

title: Eluding the chase
text: Enemies hot on your heels? To lose your tail, you have to disappear and lay low while the heat dies down.

title: Public Enemies
text: The NCPD issues bounties for some of the city's wanted criminals. If you defeat a wanted person, the city will reward you with a generous money transfer.

title: Tutorial_crafting_materials
text: To craft an item you need crafting materials. List of all needed materials is displayed on the right side. You can get crafting materials by looting and disassembling items. You can also buy them in shops

title: Tutorial_upgrading_main
text: To upgrade an item you need crafting materials. List of all needed materials is displayed on the right side. You can get crafting materials by looting and disassembling items. You can also buy them in shops

title: Skipping Rides
text: If you're riding as a passenger and nothing important is going on, you can press <Input actionName="Exit" color="MainColors.Blue" hold="Hide"></> to skip the ride and arrive immediately at your destination.

title: Hijacking Vehicles
text: Occupied vehicles can be hijacked as long as you meet the Body Attribute Requirement. Just watch out for the police – they won't let you off easy.

title: Damaging Vehicles
text: If your vehicle continues to take damage, it will eventually explode, killing everyone inside.

title: Vehicles: Buying
text:
On the AUTOFIXER netpage, you'll find all vehicles currently up for sale. You can access this netpage from the computer in your apartment or from other computers throughout Night City marked with a <Image id="UIIcon.autofixer" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> icon.

A vehicle's picture may display an icon to indicate that it comes equipped with a built-in feature:
<Image id="UIIcon.MachineGun" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> Machine Gun
<Image id="UIIcon.RocketLauncher" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> Missile Launcher
<Image id="UIIcon.VehicleCustomization" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> CrystalCoat™ customizer

As your Street Cred grows, so will the number of vehicles available to you on AUTOFIXER.

title: Equipping Quickhacks in Your Cyberdeck
text: Your cyberdeck has a limited capacity for quickhacks, but you are free to swap out which ones you have installed on it whenever you wish. To do so, go to your inventory. The Tier of the quickhack you want to install must be the same or lower than the Tier of your cyberdeck.

title: Equipping Quickhacks
text: Select the Cyberdeck slot in your inventory to open the mod screen.

title: Shooting Range
text: Shoot at the targets to score points. Try this out if you want to test weapon or just feel like unwinding.

title: Database
text: The Database contains detailed information about the people you've met, the places you've visited, the history of Night City and summaries of corporations, among other things.

title: Attributes
text:
Attributes are the most important element in building your character. Each Attribute has a unique impact on your gameplay experience. To see detailed information about a particular Attribute, hover over its icon.

Whenever you level up or climb 3 Street Cred tiers, you will gain points that can be spent on Attributes to improve them.

title: Attribute Levels
text: Each Attribute contains a set of Skills. The level of the Attribute determines the maximum level that these Skills can reach. Select an Attribute with <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to view its related Skills and the Perks within them.

title: Skills
text:
Use <Input actionName="prior_sub_menu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input actionName="next_sub_menu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to cycle through Skills and view their corresponding Perks.

By performing actions tied to specific Skills, you can become more proficient in them and gain new levels.

title: Perks
text:
Perks allow you to improve your character's stats and add new Abilities. Hover over a Perk's icon to see detailed information about it.

You gain Perk Points whenever you increase in Character Level, Skill Level, or Street Cred. You can unlock more advanced Perks after investing enough points in the Perk tree.

title: Level Up
text: You've just earned points that can be spent to level up Attributes and Perks. Open the Character menu to spend them.

title: Attributes: Leveling Up
text: To spend points to level up an Attribute, hover over it and hold <Input actionName="UI_Apply" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Perks: Leveling Up
text: To spend points to level up a Perk, hover over it and hold <Input actionName="UI_Apply" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Breach Protocol: Matrix Rows
text: The top row is activated by default at the start. Selecting a character from that row will activate the corresponding column. To send a character to the Buffer, hover over it and press <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Breach Protocol: Completion
text:
You've successfully entered the sequence for ICEpick into the Buffer. This will trigger a network-wide effect.

The RAM cost of all quickhacks has been reduced.

title: Breach Protocol: Introduction
text: In contrast to quickhacks, there is a more advanced type of hacking program known as a Breach Protocol that you can use to expose vulnerabilities in enemies, devices and Access Points.

title: Breach Protocol: Basics (2)
text: Your Buffer has limited capacity, but you can increase it as you develop your netrunner skills.

title: Breach Protocol: Basics (3)
text: Remember: A character in your Buffer is useless unless it was added in the required sequence for the daemon you wish to upload.

title: Breach Protocol: Basics (4)
text: You can only store characters from active areas in the Cod Matrix. This software allows you to activate only one column or row at a time.

title: Breach Protocol: Matrix Characters
text:
Your objective is to enter the sequence for ICEpick into the Buffer.

To add a character from the Code Matrix to the Buffer, hover over it and press <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="click" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Breach Protocol: Restarting
text: Feel free to explore the possibilities of the Breach Protocol. It will restart if you fail to upload the ICEpick daemon.

title: Vehicles: Accelerating
text: To accelerate, press <Input actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Vehicles: Steering
text:
Steer with <Input context="MovementActions" actionName="MoveX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Accelerate with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Brake with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Decelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Exiting Vehicles
text: To exit the vehicle, hold <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Exit" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

title: Hostile Situations
text: Night City is infamous for its brutality. Falling victim to crime is a common part of daily life for many Night City residents. If you come across a hostile situation in progress, it's your choice whether or not to intervene.

title: NCPD Scanner Hustles
text: The NCPD doesn't have the capacity to deal with every single crime, so they started handing out rewards for people brave enough to tackle certain types of criminal activity. You'll see them marked with the following icons: <Image id="MappinIcons.GangWatchMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>, <Image id="MappinIcons.OutpostMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>, <Image id="MappinIcons.ResourceMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>, <Image id="MappinIcons.HiddenStashMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>, <Image id="MappinIcons.SmugglersDenMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>.

title: Database of Wanted Persons
text: A database of individuals with bounties assigned to them is now available to use. You can identify these wanted persons with your scanner. Since all are wanted dead or alive, the methods you use to claim your reward are entirely up you.

title: Welcome to Cyberpunk 2077!
text:
First time in Night City? Pay close attention to the tutorials to learn more about the basic mechanics of the game.

Or, if you're already an experienced edgerunner, feel free to disable hints.

title: A Job from T-Bug
text: The task T-Bug has given you is an important step on the path to developing your netrunning skills. Be sure to complete it when you get a chance.

title: Open World
text:
Night City is a living, breathing organism that offers plenty of opportunities for exploration, so pay attention to your surroundings and check your map and phone often:

GIGS: <Image id="MappinIcons.UndiscoveredMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> are received from fixers throughout Night City. Whenever you enter a district, you'll receive a message from the local fixer with a list of available Gigs. They will also be marked on the map when you approach their location, after which you'll receive another message with details about the Gig. The Gig briefing will also be stored in your Journal.
NCPD SCANNER HUSTLES: <Image id="MappinIcons.GangWatchMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>, <Image id="MappinIcons.OutpostMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>, <Image id="MappinIcons.ResourceMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>, <Image id="MappinIcons.HiddenStashMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>, <Image id="MappinIcons.SmugglersDenMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> are jobs given by the Night City Police Department. That's right – the NCPD has started handing out rewards for mercs who do can do their dirty work, since they can't deal with every single petty crime... Or they just don't have the guts.

title: Installing a Quickhack on Your Cyberdeck
text: To install a quickhack on your cyberdeck, you need to first select it from the list. Select the Ping quickhack – it should then appear in a cyberdeck slot on the left side of your screen.

title: Tagging
text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Hold</> <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">to use your scanner.</>

title: Lethal Quickhacks
text:
<Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Hold</> <Input context="DeviceControl" actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">and aim at one of the guards.</>

<Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Use the Detonate Grenade quickhack to eliminate both guards at the same time.</>

title: Loot
text: Tapping <Input context="VisionActions" actionName="Ping" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> highlights interesting objects such as loot, stashes, devices and more.

title: Selecting Dialogue Choices
text: You can cycle through dialogue choices with <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Dialogue Choices
text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Gold dialogue options</> represent significant choices that progress the conversation.

title: Encrypted Shard
text: Some shards you find in the world will contain information hidden behind data encryption measures. To decrypt a shard, first either open it through the notification when you acquire it or find it later in the Shards tab under Journal in the main menu. Then, select CRACK SECURITY to unlock its secrets.

title: Taking Photos
text: To access photo mode, hold <Input actionName="TogglePhotoMode" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>. Photo mode can be disabled in settings.

title: Looted Cyberware
text: Cyberware you acquire in the world can be installed or sold at any ripperdoc clinic.

title: Upgrading Iconic Weapons
text:
You just acquired an Iconic weapon. Iconic weapons possess unique abilities; however, they cannot be improved with weapon mods.

With the appropriate components, Iconic weapons can be upgraded to a higher Tier, which significantly improves their power. You can do this from the Upgrades tab of the Crafting menu.

Iconic weapons can be found all over Night City. You might receive one from a friend or loot one off an enemy. It's also possible to find some simply lying in the ground or available for purchase at vendors. Some you might even craft yourself.

title: Incapacitating Enemies
text:
There are various ways to incapacitate enemies without killing them:
- Non-lethal takedowns
- Non-lethal quickhacks
- Non-lethal weapons
- EMP grenades and some combat gadgets
- Weapon mods that change damage to non-lethal

If a given weapon, combat gadget or quickhack deals non-lethal damage, it will be mentioned in the description.

title: Using Your Phone
text: To access your phone menu, press <Input actionName="PhoneInteract" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>

title: Over Substance™
text:
Body need some tweaks? Approach the mirror in your apartment or safehouse and select the [Change appearance] option.

Got some favorite threads? Create Outfits in your apartment's Wardrobe so you can change the appearance of your equipped clothing whenever you want!

title: Corpo Plaza apartment rented
text: Quality construction. Classic style. Zero compromises. Your ideal home awaits you in the heart of Night City!

title: Apartments: additional content installed
text:
EZEstates is proud to offer you four freshly vacated apartments in Night City! Make your next home in one of these fabulous locations:
-Budget-friendly netrunner pad in Northside
-Upscale Corpo Plaza suite
- Industrial loft in the Glen
- Stylish suite in Japantown
You can rent these units from our netpage or by visiting them in person.
EZEstates - Make the EZ choice!

title: Glen apartment rented
text: Where tradition meets modernity. A designer loft with an unbeatable view!

title: Japantown apartment rented
text: Where style meets character. Make yourself comfortable, stay a while, soak up the vibe.

title: Northside apartment rented
text: Authentically functional. It's not cramped, it's cosy! Hygge!

title: Skip fixer holocalls
text: You don't have to manually reject fixer holocalls. Go to Gameplay Settings and set desired holocalls – like those from fixers – to be rejected automatically.

title: Wardrobe
text:
You can change your appearance by activating a Wardrobe Outfit.

<Image id="UIIcon.TutorialWardrobeInventory" width="1221" height="185"></>

To do this, first you must create an Outfit in the Wardrobe at any of your apartments.

Then in your Inventory, you can activate the saved Outfit which will change the appearance of your equipped clothing using holographic projection technology. This does not change your equipped clothing’s stats.

title: Wardrobe
text:
You can have up to 6 Outfits saved in your Wardrobe. These can be activated and deactivated in the Outfit section of your Inventory at any time.

<Image id="UIIcon.TutorialWardrobeInventory" width="1221" height="185"></>

Activating a Wardrobe Outfit will change the appearance of the clothing you have equipped but will not change its stats. All clothing you find, receive, craft, disassemble, buy or sell will be saved in your Wardrobe’s memory.

title: The Humanity Cost
text: The cyberware upgrades are limited by the amount of points spent on attributes to which the cyberware part is related.

title: Getting the armor
text: Clothing don't give you any additional protection. You need to buy armor cyberware from ripperdocs.

text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Hold</> <Input actionName="ToggleCrouch" color="MainColors.Blue"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">to toggle crouch and move silently.</>

title: BARGHEST: Red Alert
text: To lose the BARGHEST forces chasing you, you have to get to an underground car park near the Expo Hall.

title: Point of No Return
text: This demo will end when you enter the Delamain cab. If you want to bask in the neon glow of Night City for a while longer, keep your hands off that door.

title: Fast Attacks
text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Press</> <Input actionName="MeleeAttack" context="Exploration" color="MainColors.Blue" hold="Hide"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">to perform a Fast Attack.</>

text: Continuously attacking your enemy will drain your Stamina. Fast Attacks and Strong Attacks have different Stamina costs. Your current Stamina is displayed as a yellow bar at the top of your HUD.

text: Your enemies' Strong Attacks can break your blocking stance in the same way your Strong Attacks can break theirs.

title: Attacking after Blocking
text: While holding <Input actionName="MeleeBlock" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> press <Input actionName="MeleeAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to perform an attack after blocking.

title: Final Test
text: You are equipped with a range of weapons and a cyberdeck. You will now face a mix of enemies whom you already encountered in training. <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Defeat them however you choose.</>

title: Quickhacking: Quickhack Menu
text: This is the quickhack menu. The world around you slows down while you have it open, allowing you more time to consider your quickhack selection.

title: Quickhacking: RAM Cost
text: To execute quickhacks, your cyberdeck needs to have the necessary programs installed. All quickhacks use RAM, which frees back up over time.

title: Quickhacking: Uploading Quickhacks
text:
Switch between targets with <Input actionName="UI_LookX_Axis" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Select quickhacks with <Input actionName="UI_MoveUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input actionName="UI_MoveDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Execute a quickhack with <Input actionName="UI_ApplyAndClose" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

title: Quickhacking: High RAM Cost
text: Sometimes the RAM cost of a quickhack will exceed your cyberdeck's available RAM units. In this case, you cannot execute the given quickhack or multiple quickhacks at the same time.

title: Quickhacking: ICEpick
text:
The ICEpick daemon installed on your cyberdeck can be uploaded by successfully completing a Breach Protocol.

It breaches the local network and lowers target defenses by reducing the RAM cost of quickhacks you might use against them. This allows you to use either more powerful quickhacks or a greater number of them at once.

title: Quickhacking and Breach Protocol
text:
You can select quickhacks and the Breach Protocol with <Input actionName="UI_MoveUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input actionName="UI_MoveDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.
Breach Protocol is a special program that allows you to manually hack network vulnerabilities and can help make quickhacking easier once completed.

Select Breach Protocol and press <Input actionName="UI_ApplyAndClose" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to start it now.

title: Leaning from Cover
text:
To lean from behind cover and around corners, hold <Input actionName="RangedADS" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.
Use <Input actionName="LeanLeft" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input actionName="LeanRight" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to change leaning direction.

title: Leaning from Cover with a Weapon

Change direction with  <Input actionName="LeanLeft" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input actionName="LeanRight" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Shoot with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>

title: Taking Cover
text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Press</> <Input context="Locomotion" actionName="ToggleCrouch" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">to crouch and hide behind cover.</> Cover can protect you from enemy fire.

title: Required Tutorial Complete
text: You've completed the mandatory portion of the tutorial. Feel free to interact with the door to exit the simulation, or if you wish to learn other gameplay features, check out the optional tutorials.

text: <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Hold</> <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">to activate your scanner.</>

title: Scanner: Details
text:
Scanning highlights interesting objects in your surroundings and can provide valuable information about them.
Enemies are marked <Rich color="MainColors.Red" style="Bold">Red</>, interactive objects are marked <Rich color="MainColors.Blue" style="Bold">Blue</>, and Job-related objects are marked <Rich color="MainColors.Yellow" style="Bold">Gold</>.
Hostile devices that can be hacked are colored by a digital pattern and marked with the icon <Image id="MappinIcons.HackableDeviceMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>. Neutral devices are marked <Rich color="MainColors.Hacking" style="Bold">Green</>.
Aim at the screen and press <Input actionName="OpenQuickHackPanel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to access the quickhack menu.

title: Quickhacking: RAM Cost
text: The RAM required to use a quickhack depends on the ICE level of the target you're hacking. You can increase or decrease the RAM cost, but it can never go below 1 unit.

title: Quickhacking: ICE Level
text: The ICE level of an enemy or device is calculated by halving the difference between your respective levels and adding the target's resistance. The ICEpick daemon allows you to reduce the target's resistance, thereby reducing the level of ICE.

title: Quickhacking: Taking Control of Devices
text:
Quickhacking allows you to take control of certain devices.
Hold <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to activate the scanner, then aim at the camera.

title: FIA: OPERATIONAL RECON IN “DOGTOWN”

BARGHEST - subgroup led by Ross Ulmer. Engaged in smuggling operations. Contraband regularly includes arms, drugs, cyberware and biohacking products. Large and well-armed group on site.

title: ARTHUR "CORMAC" CORMAC
text:
ARTHUR "CORMAC" CORMAC

Current Role: Fixer

Age: 41

Operates in: Wellsprings, Glen, Santo Domingo, Watson (occasionally)
Known Associates: El Sombreron, Dutch, Wesley Simms, Jago Szabó, Kiki, Myst Errya de Mort

Known Sources: Roork, Kyle J., Brisa, Dutch, The Foreman, Cholo, Kiki, The Grebe

Profile: Cooperates with a number of Night City fixers, carrying out one-off contracts within their territories. Likes to operate alone and complete gigs in person. Employs subcontractors on rare occasions, always vouching for them and staying close to the area of operations. Preferred weapon: handgun (privately trained). Wesley Simms is his go-to aide for gigs requiring netrunning skills.
Initiated contact with Jago Szabó.
Known enhancements: Subdermal Armor, Pain Editor (2071 model, oveclocked by Dutch, resuting in a 21% pain threshold enhancement).

title: Death from Above: Mass Drivers as Weapons of Mass Destruction
text:
Sixty-six million years ago, an asteroid struck our planet and changed the course of natural history. Measuring approximately 6.2 miles (10 km) in diameter, the space rock struck with a force equal to 10 billion atom bombs, leaving a crater 18.5 miles (30 km) deep. Of course, the likelihood of another such catastrophe occuring in the near future is next to none. But can we really sleep soundly at night? That all depends on the European Space Council, which currently has three Moon-based mass drivers at its disposal. That's right – three!

Researchers estimate that if the Earth were struck by an object even 50 meters in diameter, the shockwave following impact would be enough to flatten a mid-sized city. Add to that the resulting fires and tsunamis, and the number of potential victims skyrockets. On average, an asteroid of that size approaches our planet once every 1500 years. But a mass driver can launch an object of the same size once an hour!

The first – and to this day only – use of the mass driver in armed conflict took place in 2008 during the so-called First Orbital War.  In alliance with the USSR, the European Space Council used a mass driver at Tycho to launch a two-ton stone at the US Army Headquarters in Colorado Springs without warning, not only annihilating the entire general staff, but also much of the surrounding city, which had not been evacuated.

In theory, the various uses of mass drivers are now strictly regulated by law and limited only to Moon-based projects of the ESC, which in turn is theoretically an apolitical organization dealing only with matters of space exploration. But in practice, access to these monstrous cannons would give the ESC a distinct advantage in any conflict fought on Earth. If the rumors are true that Arasaka has built their own mass driver in Mare Nubium on the Moon – right under the ESC's nose – then we've already got two powerful players holding our planet in check.

Think it's not your problem? Think there's nothing to be done? Think again! Share this article, sign our petition, go to a protest or contribute to our fund to build a full planetary shield!

title: Arvin Accord Redefined?
text:
Ever since mayor Rhine declared Pacifica "an independent district", I keep wondering what it really means and what will the long-term ramifications of that decision be. Will it result in a small-scale war? 2070's Arvin Accord clearly defined Night City as free and autonomous, a result of Rhyne's efforts and political savvy. But as soon as the dust has settled, the mayor realized that some of the land he so valiantly fought for may be nothing more than dead weight as far as NC's welfare is concerned.
Dropping Pacifica from the administrative boundaries of the Free City of Night City has been a drawn-out process, since long-term action is always easier to digest by the public, but in reality, the district hasn't been considered a part of the city for a long time, by NC residents and even the NCPD, which withdrew from Pacifica years ago. But the official split came only when he needed to boost his support by massaging the crime stats.
So where did Pacifica find itself after the end of the Unification War? The Arvin Accord did not end the war, but simply moved it elsewhere without designating clear winners or losers or appeasing the ambitions of anyone involved. This is why a large independent district neighboring Night City would be a great catch for anyone vying for influence over the metropolis. The ambiguity of borders described in the Accord makes Pacifica a perfect location for everyone working in the shadows, and any kind of operations would not necessarily lead to breaking the 2070 treaty, but rather its creative reinterpretation.

title: NetWatch Claims: "We're not a RABID!"
text:
NetWatch is denying rumors that it's secretly run by the primary RABID left by Rache Bartmoss after his death. Though the accusations are serious, for now only medias of questionable credibility seem to be circulating them. But let's imagine for a minute: if an institution like NetWatch truly was one of the entities responsible for the DataKrash and demise of the old Net, then we would have to rethink everything we thought we knew about today's world.
NetWatch is the only one protecting us from the wild AIs, NetWatch is the only one tracking down whatever RABIDs remain free (of which it notes some might, and only might have any effect in realspace)… doesn't that sound like the perfect smokescreen? A simple trick that could allow the faceless (...or simply encrypted?) leadership of one of the world's most important institutions to achieve complete domination? Could NetWatch agents really be working for an AI? If all that sounds like a conspiracy theory, well... perhaps it is.
Of course, in their statement NetWatch provides numerous arguments against such theories, the foremost of which seems to be: “We've been policing the Net since 1991.” This choice of words seems a bit too soundbite-ready, yet it may serve to stem the incoming PR crisis. But if you really think about it, the statement itself doesn't prove anything.
If the RABIDs are AIs meant to imitate Bartmoss himself and carry on his "mission," then there's very little we could categorically refute. Whether we like it or not , Bartmoss was a genius, and there's no evidence we've seen the end of his plan. When it comes down to it, much remains to be seen, and in theory NetWatch could still prove to be his magnum opus.
If history has taught us anything, it's that there's no such thing as objective truth; everything is subjective, and institutions of public trust have become a thing of the past.
The question remains: will NetWatch manage to quell the rumors, or is it headed for a PR crisis? And what effect will that have on the average Net citizen? After all, it's likely we'll never get to the bottom of this netmess.

title: The Plex - A Step in the Right Direction?
text:
City governments of the east coast's metroplex, The Plex, have issued an appeal to residents of the region to register their place of residence in official NUS records. Baltimore City Council has attempted to restructure the primary school system and access to education for several years. Delaware in its entirety has struggled for months to implement waste disposal regulations. In both cases, statutory changes have stalled. Each proposal has been met with uncertainty from councilmembers and, ultimately, with legislative stagnation.

In a joint appeal, authorities emphasized the importance of statistical analyses policymaking in the metroplex. Without specific data, future improvements to existing societal detriments, ineffective decision-making, and inefficient financial investment will be significantly hindered..

According to the latest official statistical estimates, 15-40% of people residing in the Plex are not formally registered.. Problems with determining the accurate population counts along the belt are additionally exacerbated by increased migration within the Plex itself, primarily for temporary labor. To further maximize income, these individuals try to remain off official records. In other words, some individuals may be counted multiple times, and others – not at all.

Individual municipalities within the Plex, from Boston to Washington, have promised to begin negotations for increased public transportation infrastructure (especially intercity), and have begun talks about temporary, non-corporate housing options to reduce residents' dependency on their corporate employers. In doing so, city authorities expect residents to register in the government system and become involved in the development of metroplex infrastructure, which, they argue, would benefit both parties.

The appeal exhibits a spirit of freedom, demonstrates an understanding for the need to loosen the corporate tether and puts into action a plan to care for the needs of this large demographic. Of course, the appeal itself should be approached tactfully, and decisions should be weighed carefully against trusted data. But, at the very least, it appears metroplex authorities are trying to take a step in the right direction. It's possible the search for true motives may be an unnecessary distraction when the far-reachingvalue of these emerging opportunities is plain to see. After all, both sides have to remain somewhat flexible. But, for the time being, we will watch and wait as the situation develops in what is likely to be a long, drawn-out process.

title: Mr. Kipper: A Universal Message
text:
DJ, composer, producer, radio host, performer, Crystal Palace resident. Although all of the above is true, Mr. Kipper describes himself first and foremost as a Highrider. His music, on the other hand, defies all labels. The self-taught musical savant has five albums and nine EPs to his credit, all of which have helped skyrocket his popularity throughout the solar system.

Mr. Kipper's latest singles, "Choke Hold" and "Rolla", immediately took over the "Top 10 Thumpers of the Month" list put out by interplanetary radio station Dark Star. "I communicate through rhythm", explained the artist. "It's the only language we can all understand without need of translation software." Judging by the turnout on Mr. Kipper's recent Earth tour, it certainly seems his message is getting through loud and clear.

Mr. Kipper told us that he bellieves his set lists are much more than a dynamic mix of styles and genres. "Every sound carries meaning – a call for freedom." This proud Highrider, with liquified stardust pumping through his veins, values freedom of thought and expression above all else. Mr. Kipper's newly established terrestrial radio station, 99.9 Impulse, is a medium that he believes will unite listeners across and beyond all boundaries – the same boundaries he himself has already transcended.

title: Private Press: Who, Where, and When?
text:
Just what do the faces under those iconic epoxy space helmets look like? Members of the DJ duo Private Press, Adam Brocki and Jan Wóycicki, have long refused to reveal their identities. All we know for sure is that they both hail from Grobel Orbital Station, thousands of miles from Earth.

The duo identify with the cultural heritage of the Highriders, which has proved an inexhaustible source of inspiration for their craft. Brocki explained how he felt they were "incredibly lucky to be born at a time and place that is such a rich amalgam of terrestrial and extraterrestrial influences." With a twinkle in his visor, Wóycicki added: "In space, our neurons collide at the speed of sound."

Through what feels like a paradox of space-time itself, Private Press have managed to somehow imbue their music with a freshness that also has staying power. Their latest set, created for 99.9 Impulse in collaboration with cosmic music scene megastar Mr. Kipper, is thumping in clubs from Melbourne to Lima. Audiences have raved over the experimental, expressive sound that dazzles, hypnotizes and has you feeling like you're floating in zero-g.

When asked about their plans for the near future, Brocki and Wóycicki kept us guessing with their ever-present poker faces. "Time is a flat circle," Brocki finally said. Sensing our confusion, Wóycicki offered some "clarity" on the duo's future: "We won't be leaving Earth's orbit anytime soon."
